verdict.line: You lose if Garen lands Q's silence into a level 6+ all-in while you're already under half HP; you win almost every trade once E is up and his Q is down.

brief.thesis: Darius's E (Apprehend) is the one tool in this matchup Garen has no answer for — it drags him back into range and removes his ability to disengage from a fight he's losing, while Darius's passive (Hemorrhage) stacking wins any extended trade Garen agrees to. Garen's only real counters are landing Q's silence before Darius starts his combo, and burying him with R (Demacian Justice) once level 6 hits. Outside of those two windows, Darius simply out-trades him.

theirWindow.when: Level 6+ with Q and R both up
theirWindow.what: Once Garen hits level 6 his all-in spikes hard: Q silences you so you can't E, W, or R back, E (Judgment) shreds your armor, and R executes a big chunk of true damage off missing health. If you're below ~60% HP and he has Q and R both available, disengage instead of trading — you cannot out-silence a silence.

yourWindow.what: The moment you have E, look to pull Garen mid-wave while his Q is on cooldown — without the silence he has no way to interrupt your E into W into auto into Q sequence, and your passive stacks snowball the trade decisively in your favor.

start.why: The lifesteal rewards fighting often and offsets Garen's own out-of-combat passive regen (Perseverance) during early skirmishes.

boots.why: Every point of Garen's damage is physical — autos, E (Judgment) spin, and R — so flat armor blunts his entire kit, not just one instance.

core.why: Gives the burst, attack speed, and movement speed to land E into W into auto into Q before he can spin away or reposition.
Stacks armor shred on top of Garen's own E shred, letting your true damage and autos punch through whatever tank items he buys.
The HP and damage-scaling shield keeps you alive through his Q silence window and stops a single burst rotation from finishing you.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained trading and extended all-ins that Darius wants — stack it during your E-W-auto-Q sequence and the healing offsets Garen's own sustain.

playing.title: Trade Only After E
playing.detail: Don't commit with just Q or W before level 2 — without E you can't stop Garen from walking away or punishing you with his own Q silence.

playing.title: Pull Mid-Wave, Not Immediately
playing.detail: Land E when minions are near so he can't cleanly disengage, and time it for when his Q (Decisive Strike) is on cooldown so he has no silence to interrupt your combo.

playing.title: Stack Passive Before Committing R
playing.detail: Land Q edge hits and autos to build 5 stacks of Hemorrhage first — your R's execute threshold and true damage jump hugely at max stacks.

playing.title: Respect The Level 6 Spike
playing.detail: Once Garen hits 6, don't stand in melee range below roughly 60% HP; his Q into E into R can kill through a CS lead if he lands the silence first.

playing.title: Watch For The Silence Tell
playing.detail: Garen must activate Q before his next auto silences — if you see that buff icon light up, back off or bait it out rather than eating a free silence into his all-in.

playing.title: Ignite Breaks His Sustain
playing.detail: Garen's passive heals him hard out of combat between skirmishes — Ignite removes that safety net and makes every trade you win stick.

playing.title: Don't Chase Under Turret
playing.detail: His E and R reward him for standing and fighting, not fleeing, so if he dives under his tower to reset, let him go instead of trading into tower shots plus a spin.

verdict.line: You lose lane if you auto-attack into his Counter Strike (Q) or get caught overextended right as he hits 6; you win every extended trade and side-lane split once you have two items.

brief.thesis: Fiora's W (Riposte) directly answers the two tools Jax uses to force trades — the Empowered Strike (E) auto and the Leap Strike (Q) gap-close — while his Counter Strike (Q) only punishes basic attacks, not her dash-based poke. Because of that asymmetry, this lane is decided by who initiates the exchange, not by stats: if you lead with Q (Lunge) or bait his dodge window instead of auto-attacking blind, you take almost no free damage from him.

theirWindow.what: Grandmaster's Might (R) gives him burst armor/MR plus an AoE stun on activation, and paired with a Leap Strike (Q) into Empowered Strike (E) he can chain a stun into a kill. Don't stand in melee range with your Flash down at this window.

yourWindow.when: right after his Counter Strike (Q) whiffs or ends
yourWindow.what: Counter Strike has a real cooldown (roughly 14s at rank 1, shorter at rank 5), so once it's down he has no stun and no dodge. All-in immediately with Q (Lunge) into E (Bladework) for the double empowered autos onto his revealed vital.

boots.why: Jax's damage is heavily auto-attack based (passive stacks, Empowered Strike autos), so the flat auto-attack damage reduction directly cuts his all-in and his late-game on-hit scaling.

playing.title: Never auto into Counter Strike
playing.detail: When Jax activates Q (Counter Strike) he dodges the next two seconds of basic attacks and then stuns anyone nearby. Stop auto-attacking the instant you see it trigger and poke with Q (Lunge) instead.

playing.title: Watch his E icon for empowered autos
playing.detail: Jax's E (Empowered Strike) primes his next basic attack to deal bonus magic damage, and it stuns if that auto follows a Leap Strike (Q) engage. If his E is up and he jumps on you, riposte the incoming auto with W.

playing.title: Riposte the leap-strike follow-up
playing.detail: Time W (Riposte) for the auto that lands right after his Q (Leap Strike) engage — parrying it both denies his stun and stuns him back, flipping the trade entirely.

playing.title: Respect the level 6 all-in window
playing.detail: Grandmaster's Might gives him burst armor/MR and an AoE stun on activation. From level 6 on, don't sit in melee range below 60% HP with your Flash and W both down.

playing.title: Chain E into vital resets
playing.detail: Use E (Bladework) to guarantee two empowered autos onto his revealed vital for true damage and the attack-speed/heal proc; do this every short trade, not just all-ins.

playing.title: Punish Counter Strike cooldown
playing.detail: Once he burns Counter Strike defensively, it's down for roughly 14 seconds early and shorter at higher ranks. That's your green light to force an all-in with no stun risk from him.

playing.title: Split-push once you have two items
playing.detail: Past Trinity Force and Bloodthirster you out-duel Jax 1v1 even through his ultimate. Prioritize side-lane splits so your ultimate (Grand Challenge) rewards you with true damage in isolated fights.

verdict.line: You win the early levels and every Realm of Death you time correctly; he wins any fight where you let his resistances stay stacked.

brief.thesis: K'Sante is a resistance-stacking tank whose passive proc scales off his own bonus armor and magic resist, so flat AP does very little into him — you beat him with percent-max-health magic damage and magic penetration, never with burst. The flip side is that your R (Realm of Death) steals a percentage of his stats, so ulting him doesn't just remove the enemy frontline for seven seconds, it lets you wear his tankiness while you do it. That stat theft, not the lane, is the real win condition in this matchup.

yourWindow.when: W spent, or he is mid-Q animation
yourWindow.what: This is when Q actually lands for full value and E can drag him where you want him. Everything you want from a trade happens in the few seconds after Path Maker goes down.

brief.thesis: Olaf's E (Reckless Swing) is true damage to both of you, so stacking armor doesn't make trading into him free the way it does against most top laners. Worse, his R (Ragnarok) grants immunity to all disables, which directly no-sells the two abilities your whole kit is built around — E (Facebreaker)'s stun and R (The Show Stopper)'s suppression grab simply fail to lock him down while it's active. This matchup is decided by whether you fight on your cooldown timers or his.

theirWindow.what: Do not commit E (Facebreaker) or R (The Show Stopper) — both fail against his CC immunity and he gets bonus attack speed to punish the whiff. Poke with Q (Knuckle Down) and autos only, and bait the ult out with a half-commit before going in.

yourWindow.what: This is when your grab actually lands. Full commit: W (Haymaker) for the shield and slow, E (Facebreaker) into a wall for the stun, empowered Grit auto, then R (The Show Stopper) to close it out.

playing.detail: Ragnarok makes your E and R whiff entirely. Never commit the grab combo while it's up — poke instead and wait him out.

playing.title: Don't auto-trade through Reckless Swing
playing.detail: His E is true damage on top of his own self-damage, meaning he's willing to burn health you can't mitigate with armor. Disengage rather than match autos.

playing.title: Land E into terrain
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if you throw him into a wall; without one he's just tossed behind you with zero CC applied.

playing.title: Watch for his axe on the ground
playing.detail: Undertow leaves a pickup axe that refunds cooldown — if it's still sitting there, his kit is running on longer timers and he's weaker to engage.

playing.title: Time all-ins to your Grit bar
playing.detail: Once the Grit meter under your health bar is full, your next auto becomes an empowered haymaker — hold the engage a half-second to land it inside the stun window.

playing.title: Don't Flash to chase during his ult
playing.detail: He's immune to slows and gets bonus attack speed during Ragnarok, so trying to stick with Flash just wastes it. Disengage and punish him after it ends instead.

playing.title: Force the level 3-5 kill lane
playing.detail: This is your clearest advantage window before his R exists — commit Ignite-backed all-ins here rather than passing up the lane.

brief.thesis: Renekton is one of the hardest early lane bullies in the game and Sett is one of the better late-game bruisers, so this lane is entirely about surviving levels 1–5. The saving grace is that Sett's W converts damage taken into grit while Renekton's all-in is front-loaded burst — his combo literally loads your gun. Most Setts lose this matchup by trying to trade first instead of letting him commit and W'ing back.
